newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco arrests 4 Colombians for $500 mln cocaine.
newsitem.headline: Morocco arrests 4 Colombians for $500 mln cocaine.

text.p: Moroccan police have arrested four Colombians for drug trafficking and seized a former British ship involved in smuggling six tonnes of pure cocaine valued at $500 million, a South American diplomat said on Thursday.
The cocaine was washed up on Morocco's Atlantic coast last month.

"Four Colombians travelling with false Panamanean passports were arrested in Kenitra port and charged with cocaine trafficking...They will soon appear before local court," the diplomat, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
Kenitra is located on the Atlantic coast 35 km (20 miles) north of Rabat.
Moroccan interior ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
Earlier this month the official MAP news agency reported that security forces had seized six tonnes of pure cocaine worth more than $500 million which washed up on beaches over several days.
The first cocaine was discovered last month by children playing on a Casablanca beach when they opened plastic bags and tasted the white powder inside.

Initial investigations suggested it was thrown overboard when an old ship taking it to southern Europe "broke down and missed a rendezvous" with a vessel due to run it to the Portuguese-Spanish coast, MAP said.

"The ship named Adunas, which is seized by Moroccan police in Kenitra, belonged to the British Royal Navy and was bought earlier this year by private individuals in the United Kingdom for $340,000 cash. It was registered in Belize," the diplomat said.
The ship in April visited Morocco's southern city of Agadir with six passengers on board, including two Spaniards and four Colombians, the diplomat said.
In June it sailed for the Canary Islands where the crew took on board the cocaine bound for southern Europe, he said.
On its way to southern Spain, the ship "had engine trouble near Casablanca coast...It called for urgent assistance which was granted by Moroccans", the diplomat said.
The drug cargo was thrown overboard before the arrival of Moroccan patrol units to rescue the ship, he added.

Morocco's interior ministry on Tuesday held a meeting with experts from France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Germany, Britain and United States to discuss the seized cocaine and its international implications, MAP had said but gave no details.

Morocco has shown itself particularly concerned in the past two years over drug trafficking which has focused largely on cannabis, much of it produced in the north of the African country just across the Mediterranean from Spain.

Morocco launched a crackdown on drug smuggling last year, and the interior minister said recently it had seized 103 tonnes of cannabis and more than 100 kgs (220 pounds) of cocaine bound for Europe in 1996. It had also arrested more than 18,000 drug traffickers, including 342 foreigners.
